newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse ends session slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse ends session slightly lower.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed on Thursday 0.06 percent lower pulled down slightly by a drop of the market's largest capitalisation firms, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index closed at 474.02 points, down from 474.25 points on Wednesday.
"The bourse index decline compared with Wednesday's session is a normal adjustment...The drop in share values of market blue chips have slightly affected the market," a trader said.
A block of more than 30,000 shares were exchanged on the official market worth 26 million dirhams, the trader added.
ONA group, the country's largest private group, fell three dirhams to close at 590 dirhams.
Its subsidiary Centrale Laitiere, which gained 56 dirhams on the previous session, was not traded on Thursday.
Societe Nationale d'Investissment, Morocco's second largest conglomerate, lost 10 dirhams in one session to close at 555 dirhams.
SNI has diversified stakes in more than 40 companies and a market capitalisation of 5.5 billion dirhams.
Leading cement firm Ciments de l'Oriental, was traded at 479 dirhams, down 11 dirhams on the previous session.
The firm holds nearly 20 percent of cement sales and was expected to publish a good results for 1996, a Casablanca-based broker said.
Among the rising stocks was Wafabank which gained 17 dirhams in one session to close at 597 dirhams.

Wafabank decided to buy 100 percent of Spanish Uniban bank or more than 2.46 million shares priced at around $28 million. The effective absorption of Uniban by Wafabank is expected to take place by end March 1997, officials said.
Total traded volume on the official market was 31.6 million dirhams against 36.7 million dirhams on Wednesday.
